en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa-kanda
1. The Training Rule on Litigiousness.
Now, venerable ladies, these seventeen rules on formal meeting of the Saṅgha come up for recitation.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain lay follower, having given a storehouse to the community of bhikkhunīs, passed away.
He had two sons:
one was faithless and lacked conviction, while the other was faithful and possessed conviction.
They divided their paternal inheritance.
Then that one who was faithless and lacked confidence said this to the one who was faithful and possessed confidence:
"There is our storehouse; let us divide it."
When this was said, the one who was faithful and confident said this to the one who lacked faith and confidence:
“Do not speak thus, noble lady.
Our father gave [it] to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.”
A second time, that one who was faithless and without confidence said this to the one who was faithful and confident:
"Our granary; let us divide it.
Then, that one who was faithful and confident said this to the one who was faithless and without confidence:
“Noble ladies, do not speak thus.
This was given to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs by our father.
A third time, that one who lacked faith and confidence said this to her who had faith and confidence:
“Let us divide our storehouse.
Then that faithful and devout man thought,
“If it should belong to me, I too shall give it to the community of nuns.”
He said this to that person who was faithless and lacked confidence:
"Let us divide [the goods].
Then, as that storehouse was being divided by them, it fell to the share of that faithless and unconfident man.
Then that man, lacking faith and lacking confidence, approached the bhikkhunīs and said this:
"Come out, noble ladies; our storehouse is ready.
When this was said, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to that man:
“Ladies, do not speak thus; it was given to the community of bhikkhunīs by your father.
They asked the chief ministers of justice, “Was it given, or was it not given?
The ministers replied as follows:
“Noble lady, who knows that it has been given to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs?
When this was said, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to those chief ministers:
“Have you ever seen or heard of a gift being given while a witness is appointed, noble sirs?”
Then those high officials,
thinking, "What the noble ladies have said is indeed true," made that storehouse over to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.
Thereupon, that defeated man complained, grumbled, and became indignant.
“These women are no longer ascetics; they are shaven-headed harlots.
How can they possibly have our storehouse confiscated?
Thus did the bhikkhunī Thullanandā inform the high officials of this matter.
The high officials had that man punished.
Then, having been punished, that man had a lodging for Ājīvakas constructed not far from the nuns' quarters and dispatched the Ājīvakas, saying:
"Address these nuns with harsh words."
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā informed the high officials of this matter.
The high officials had that man bound.
People criticized, complained, and spread it about:
“First they had the nuns take away the grain-storage shed; secondly, they had them fined; thirdly, they had them bound;
now they will have them executed.
The nuns heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires … [as before] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā live as one who brings lawsuits?
Then those bhikkhunīs informed the bhikkhus of this matter … [as before] …
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā lives as one who brings lawsuits?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her … [as before] …
“How, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā live as one who brings about legal disputes?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:”
“Whatever bhikkhunī should live as a litigant with a householder, or a householder’s son, or a slave, or a laborer,
or even with a renunciant wanderer— this bhikkhunī has committed an offense that is an immediate offense, involving expulsion, a *saṅghādisesa*.”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before]... nun.
...pe... this is the nun intended in this context.
One who is called a litigant is said to be one who causes legal disputes.
A householder (gahapati) is anyone who dwells in a home.
A householder’s son (gahapatiputta) is...
Whosoever [are] sons or brothers;
a slave is one born in the house, one purchased with wealth, or one brought as a captive.
A laborer means a hired servant or one who has been brought into service.
A recluse and wanderer means...
Except for a bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a sikkhamānā, a sāmaṇera, or a sāmaṇerī, anyone who has entered the order of wanderers:
if one seeks out a second person or goes with the intention, "I will make a wager," it is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one informs a single person, it is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one informs a second person, there is an offense of thullaccaya.
At the conclusion of half [the recitation], there is an offense of saṅghādisesa.
This is an offense of immediate commission.
One incurs [this offense] together with the transgression of the subject matter by means of not having been formally admonished.
"Leading to expulsion" means that one is expelled from the Saṅgha.
“Saṅghādisesa”:
it is the Saṅgha alone that grants the *mānatta* penance for that offense, sends one back to the beginning, or rehabilitates one; it is not a number of monks, nor a single bhikkhunī.
Therefore it is called “an offense entailing suspension from the Saṅgha. It is the designation and synonym for that very class of offenses; for that reason also it is called “saṅghādisesa.”
There is no offense if she goes while being dragged away by people,
or if she asks for protection.
If she points it out without specifying [the person], if she is insane, ... [and so on] ...
for one who is a first-time offender.
The first Saṅghādisesa training rule is finished.
